diff.title: Bulk storage in Zone B
diff.before:
1. Operate Zone B strictly as the bulk storage zone with high-bay pallet racking under PR-02 Put-away to storage.
2. Store all reserve and bulk stock inside the high-bay racking, which provides 2,400 pallet positions.
3. Place only one pallet identifier per rack position and confirm the booking with the WMS scanner before leaving the bay.
4. Respect the structural limit of each rack bay at all times; each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
5. Verify pallet weight before lifting to the beams, because a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
6. Split any consignment that would overload a single bay across two or more bays in the same aisle.
7. Use only the assigned reach trucks for all high-bay movements; the fleet provides 4 reach trucks for the high bays.
8. Observe the rated capacity of the reach trucks at 1.6 t and never attempt to lift heavier unit loads with them.
9. Assign Forklift operators trained on reach trucks to Zone B put-away and retrieval tasks.
10. Keep Stock controllers responsible for monitoring bay utilisation and reporting overloads or damage immediately.
11. Maintain main transport aisles through Zone B at 4.0 m wide and keep them completely clear of staged pallets, wrapping material and handling equipment.
12. Maintain rack storage aisles at 3.0 m wide and prohibit parking or double-staging inside them during put-away.
13. Drive at walking pace when entering a storage aisle and yield to a reach truck already positioned at a bay face.
14. Apply free block stacking only in marked floor areas outside the racking and never inside the storage aisles.
15. Limit any free block stack to 3 pallets high.
16. Limit any free block stack to 4.0 m in height, even where three low pallets would remain below that height.
17. Check stack stability, pallet quality and load overhang before adding the second or third pallet.
18. Report leaning stacks, broken boards or shifted loads to the shift supervisor and do not add further pallets to an unstable stack.
19. Return damaged pallets to the designated area and re-palletise the goods before returning them to Zone B.
20. Complete every put-away under PR-02 Put-away to storage by scanning the final bay location so inventory accuracy remains intact for replenishment and picking.

Zone B feeds the ground-level pick faces in the adjacent zone. Accurate bay discipline here prevents shortages, double handling and unsafe overloads downstream.

Coordinate with maintenance staff when rack impact, bent beams or missing safety pins are found. Isolate the affected bay until it has been inspected and released back to use.

diff.title: Pallet weight and trailer capacity
diff.before:
1. Apply a single maximum pallet weight to every outbound load plan. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Use this figure as the planning weight for stability checks, weight totals and transport bookings, even when the actual pallet weighs less.

Assess each order against that limit before wrapping and staging. Reject overweight pallets for rework into compliant units. Record the verified weight in the release documentation covered under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

2. Plan curtain-side trailer loads against payload first. Our contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg. Divide that payload by the maximum pallet weight to establish the weight-constrained limit.

Calculate 24000 kg divided by 1000 kg per pallet to give 24 pallets. Treat this quotient as a hard ceiling for full-weight pallets. Do not round upward or add an additional pallet on the assumption of lighter average weight without a documented re-weigh.

3. Compare the weight result with the physical floor capacity. A trailer has 33 floor pallet positions. Position count sets the volume footprint available for standard pallets placed on the trailer bed.

Count positions from the headboard to the rear doors without double-stacking unless the load plan expressly permits it. Leave damaged floor sections empty and reduce the usable count accordingly.

4. Govern every full-weight movement by the lower of the two limits. A trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets (payload divided by maximum pallet weight, capped by floor positions).

Explain the outcome to loading teams in plain terms. Weight restricts the load before space does. Nine floor positions remain theoretically vacant when carrying 24 pallets at 1000 kg each, because adding a 25th full-weight pallet would exceed the 24000 kg payload.

5. Build mixed-weight loads within the same ceiling. Sum the actual verified weights of all pallets on the consignment. Keep the total at or below 24000 kg and the pallet count at or below 33 floor pallet positions.

Allocate heavier pallets over the axles and distribute weight evenly along the bed. Secure each row to prevent shifting during transit. Reconcile the final loaded quantity and weight against the release paperwork before closing the doors.

6. Document exceptions and partial loads consistently. Where pallets weigh less than 1000 kg, more than 24 physical pallets may travel provided neither the 24000 kg payload nor the 33 floor pallet positions are exceeded.

Enter the per-pallet weights, total weight and position count on the load sheet. Retain the calculation for audit and driver handover. Escalate any request to exceed either limit through the normal dispatch control before loading.

7. Enforce the limit at staging and loading. Check pallet weights at wrapping, verify totals at staging, and re-confirm before truck departure. Refuse to load a 25th full-weight pallet onto a trailer already carrying 24 pallets at maximum weight, even where empty floor space remains visible.

diff.title: Van and shift dispatch limit
diff.before:
1. Use the delivery van only for small consignments that cannot justify a trailer movement. Our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg.
2. Plan van loading against floor space as well as weight. The delivery van has 6 pallet positions.
3. Apply the full-weight limit as the binding constraint for heavy pallets. The van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
4. Assign any order exceeding the van limit to trailer transport under PR-06 Outbound dispatch. Do not split a heavy pallet across van positions to circumvent the weight limit.
5. Stage van consignments in Zone D separately from trailer staging. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
6. Release van departures through the same dispatch control as trailers. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.
7. Treat the van as overflow and urban-drop capacity, not as part of the per-shift pallet promise. Record van pallets separately from trailer load counts in the release documentation.
8. Plan trailer throughput from fixed door capacity. There are 4 outbound dock doors.
9. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. No inbound receiving may occupy these doors during scheduled outbound loading.
10. Schedule loading to the standard turnaround. Each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
11. Calculate the shift promise from doors multiplied by loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift (doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer).
12. Commit to customers only within that ceiling. Accept additional bookings for the same shift only when a booked load cancels and the dispatcher releases the door slot.
13. Sequence staging, wrapping checks and reconciliation so each door completes its 3 loads without queuing into the next shift. Hold late-arriving trailers for the following shift rather than overloading doors, labour or yard space.
14. Coordinate van movements so they do not block trailer access to docks 5-8. Load the van from the marked staging area and dispatch it between trailer manoeuvres.
15. Report any door taken out of service, trailer rejection or labour shortfall to the dispatcher immediately. Reduce the promised pallet quantity for that shift pro rata and rebook the balance.

diff.title: Hazmat cage pallet limit
diff.before:
1. Store no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat in the hazmat cage at one time.
2. Treat the 4,000 kg limit as absolute for all classified stock combined, regardless of packaging type or dwell time.
3. Apply a maximum gross weight of 1000 kg to every pallet, including its load, before assessing cage capacity.
4. Derive cage pallet capacity by dividing the hazmat stock limit by the maximum pallet weight.
5. Hold at most 4 full-weight pallets in the hazmat cage at any moment.

Locate the hazmat cage inside Zone F. Operate all receipts, storage and issues under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Confine the fenced installation to its defined footprint of 60 m2.

6. Plan inbound put-away against remaining weight allowance rather than visible floor space.
7. Weigh any doubtful pallet on calibrated equipment before admission to the cage.
8. Reject admission when the next pallet would push total cage content above 4,000 kg.
9. Stage the excess quantity outside the cage in approved holding only until weight allowance becomes available.
10. Record every movement in and out by weight so the live total remains visible.
11. Reduce pallet count below 4 where individual pallets approach 1000 kg and combined weight nears the ceiling.
12. Permit more than 4 physical pallets only where documented lighter weights keep the combined total at or below 4,000 kg.
13. Count mixed full-weight and part-weight loads together toward the same limit.
14. Never use the 60 m2 floor area as justification for exceeding the weight ceiling.

Inside Zone F, segregation remains mandatory even when the cage holds fewer than 4 full-weight pallets. Maintain separation from incompatible classes, keep aisles clear for inspection, and preserve access to spill equipment at all times.

15. Check cage total before accepting a transfer from receiving, replenishment or returns.
16. Withdraw or consume existing stock first when an incoming hazmat delivery would otherwise breach the limit.
17. Escalate immediately where committed orders and on-hand stock together exceed available allowance.
18. Document weight calculations on the stock record to show division of the hazmat stock limit by the maximum pallet weight.
19. Audit the cage total at each transaction and correct discrepancies before further put-away.
20. Enforce the 4 full-weight pallet rule during shift changes, overtime working and peak inbound periods without exception.

diff.title: Driver authorisation and truck checks
diff.before:
1. Operate material-handling equipment only under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and only if you are an authorised operator. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

2. Obtain authorisation before driving any powered truck. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

3. Remember that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Do not permit unauthorised driving, passengers, or use of a truck reported as faulty.

4. Know the fleet you are assigned to. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.

5. Select the correct truck for high-bay work. The fleet has 4 reach trucks for the high bays. Reach trucks are rated at 1.6 t.

6. Use pedestrian equipment only within its design purpose. The fleet has 8 electric pallet jacks. The site has 12 hand pallet jacks.

7. Respect the rated capacity on every lift. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Never exceed the data-plate capacity of the truck in use.

8. Complete the documented pre-use check each day before starting work. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day. The daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.

9. Record brakes, steering, tyres and wheels, forks and mast, chains, horn, lights, beacon, reverse alarm, mirrors, seat belt and guarding, battery charge and leaks, hydraulic oil level and leaks, and emergency stop where fitted. Remove a defective truck from service immediately, tag it clearly, and hand the checklist to supervision.

10. Report every fault for repair without delay. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Do not restart a truck taken out of service until it has been cleared.

11. Fasten the seat belt before moving off. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving. Keep body parts inside the cage, apply the parking brake when leaving the seat, and lower the forks when parked.

12. Drive at a speed that always allows safe stopping. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.

13. Keep to a safe pace outside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

14. Slow early for people and level changes. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

15. Park only in designated areas, switch off, and secure the key. Leave keys only through the authorised handover arrangement and never lend an authorised truck to an unauthorised person.

diff.title: Racking and stacking limits
diff.before:
1. Respect the rated limits of all storage structures in Zone B. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Never place more weight or height on racking or floor stacks than this instruction allows, and never climb on racking to reach stock.

2. Limit each rack bay to at most 2,700 kg total load. Calculate the bay total from the gross weight of every pallet level within that bay before putting away the next pallet. Distribute heavy pallets to lower levels where the rack design requires it, and leave any bay showing deflection, cracking or impact damage unloaded until cleared.

3. Keep every pallet within its gross weight allowance. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Check the system weight or weigh indication before put-away and before replenishment. Reject overweight, unstable or overhanging pallets for rework and do not place them into high-bay positions.

4. Stack free block-stacked pallets only to the permitted height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high. Apply both limits together, so the lower of the two controls the stack. Build stacks square, interlocked and on sound pallets, with heavier units at the base.

5. Maintain clear operating clearances around racking at all times. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide. Do not stage pallets, waste, chargers or handling equipment inside these aisles. Keep pallet overhang, stretch film tails and loose strapping outside the aisle profile.

6. Operate handling equipment in racking strictly under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Approach bays squarely, lift and lower smoothly, and confirm adequate headroom before raising a load to height. Stop work immediately if the truck contacts uprights, beams or bracing, barrier off the affected bay, and report the impact without delay.

7. Support the monthly integrity regime for racking. Racking gets a documented safety inspection every month. The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs. Report bent uprights, missing safety pins, damaged beams, loose floor fixings and leaking goods to supervision on the same shift, and do not reload a quarantined bay.

8. Treat any suspect stack as unsafe until examined. Re-stack leaning columns, re-wrap loose loads, and transfer damaged pallets to quarantine under escort. Never pull a pallet from the bottom of a block stack, never stand pallets on edge against racking, and never leave a raised load unattended in the aisle.

diff.title: Hazmat storage rules
diff.before:
1. Confine all classified hazardous goods to the fenced hazmat cage inside Zone F. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Undertake no hazmat storage elsewhere on site.

2. Recognise the physical limits of the cage. Inside Zone F the hazmat cage covers 60 m2. Plan all receipts, put-away and picking around that footprint. Keep access routes, operating clearance and emergency access free at all times.

3. Observe the maximum stock for the cage without exception. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time. Check the current cage total before accepting any new receipt. Reject or hold back any delivery that would breach the limit.

4. Convert the weight limit into pallet spaces during planning. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. On that basis the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets. Treat lighter pallets by their actual recorded weight rather than by count alone.

5. Wear the required personal protection for every entry and every handling task around the cage. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Add any task-specific protection required by the product label and safety data sheet.

6. Execute all storage, movement and documentation under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Inspect containers for leaks, damage and correct labelling before put-away. Secure incompatible products apart using the provided segregation provisions. Keep labels facing outward for identification during checks.

7. Maintain strict order inside the 60 m2 enclosure. Place only sealed, labelled and stable units in their designated positions. Stack nothing against fencing, doors or safety equipment. Remove empty pallets, waste packaging and unused equipment without delay. Report damaged containers, missing labels or faulty fittings for immediate action under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.

8. Accept accountability at site level. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate overstock risk, unauthorised access, repeated labelling failures or any doubt about classification before continuing work. Leave the cage in a safe, closed and clearly signed condition after each activity.

Remove empty pallets, waste packaging and unused equipment without delay. Report damaged containers, missing labels or faulty fittings for immediate action under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.

diff.title: Dispatchers
diff.before:
1. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads across all staffed shifts.
2. As scheduling owner, the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers and maintains the daily transport plan without gaps or double bookings.
3. Within Zone D, the dispatch zone, outbound staging in front of docks 5-8 remains under dispatcher control from pallet staging through loading to departure.
4. Coordination with Zone A covers the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection, ensuring inbound arrivals do not conflict with outbound movements.
5. Across the building the dispatcher manages all 8 dock doors as a single resource, with dock doors 1-4 serving inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serving outbound dispatch.
6. Under PR-01 Inbound receiving, dispatchers sequence arrivals so the document check happens BEFORE unloading, and no vehicle is called to doors 1-4 without complete booking documentation.
7. Under PR-06 Outbound dispatch, dispatchers authorise each load release only when wrapping, labelling, quantity reconciliation and transport documents are complete.
8. Capacity planning uses fixed outbound throughput: there are 4 outbound dock doors and each outbound door handles 3 trailer loads per shift.
9. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for planning carry a payload of 24000 kg and provide 33 floor pallet positions for load building.
10. For full-weight planning, a trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets, calculated as payload divided by maximum pallet weight and capped by floor positions.
11. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg, and the dispatcher rejects any load plan exceeding trailer payload or floor positions.
12. Local deliveries allocated to the van respect its limits: our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg with 6 pallet positions, and takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.
13. Total outbound capacity is at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift, derived from doors x loads per shift x pallets per trailer, and dispatchers cap bookings at that ceiling.
14. Throughout the shift dispatchers work beside the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, escalating labour shortfalls, door faults and trailer rejections without delay.
15. Final accountability for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs rests with the warehouse manager, and dispatchers obtain required approvals for overtime, over-capacity bookings or exceptional movements.
16. At shift change dispatchers contribute load status, door allocation and carrier ETAs to PR-15 End-of-shift handover and remain available until the incoming team accepts control.

diff.title: Inbound Operators
diff.before:
1. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving from document check to system booking.

Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Operators report for their assigned shift, either Shift 1 which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

2. Before any trailer is opened, verify the booking, delivery note and purchase order quantity against the scheduled load.

At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading. Do not start unloading where documents are missing, quantities disagree or damage is visible from outside until the exception has been escalated under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

3. During unloading, count every carton and pallet, check outer packaging condition, labels and expiry dates where applicable, and segregate quantity variances and visible damage.

Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system. Record inspection results in the WMS and on the delivery paperwork without delay.

4. Operate pallet handling equipment within the receiving area to move inbound pallets to inspection and booking lanes, keeping pedestrian routes and dock approaches clear at all times.

Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Sign out a scanner at shift start, confirm each booking scan, and return the unit for charging at shift end.

5. Book inspected goods into the system immediately after inspection, print or activate pallet labels, and confirm weight and dimensions.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Reject overweight or unstable pallets for rework before booking.

6. Stage booked pallets by destination for release to PR-02 Put-away to storage.

Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Direct general pallets for Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Direct chilled pallets for Zone E, which is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Direct value-added, quarantine and returns-related receipts for Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

7. Hand over staged stock to forklift operators for put-away only after system booking is complete, ensuring each pallet carries its identifier and destination.

Never release unbooked goods to storage aisles or dispatch areas.

8. Wear prescribed personal protective equipment throughout all receiving work.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

9. Work under the direction of the shift team structure at all times.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow tasking, report variances, damage and missing documents immediately, and request reassignment before leaving Zone A. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

diff.title: Forklift Operators
diff.before:
Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks. The role covers pallet movements between receiving, storage, picking, dispatch and value-added areas under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

1. Operate only after authorisation. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators. No operator starts unsupervised truck work without that authorisation recorded.
2. Complete the documented pre-use check each day. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day, and the daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.
3. Operate the assigned fleet within rated capacity. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 2.5 t, 4 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 1.6 t, 8 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks.
4. Observe site speed limits at all times. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building. Forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
5. Slow for people and ramps. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
6. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Give way on segregated pedestrian walkways which are 1.2 m wide, keep clear of walkway markings, and use the 4.0 m wide main transport aisles for travel and the 3.0 m wide rack storage aisles only at controlled speed.
7. Wear mandatory personal protection on the floor. High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving.
8. Execute put-away and replenishment moves to instruction. Follow PR-02 Put-away to storage for transfers from Zone A to Zone B, and PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces for transfers from bulk storage to Zone C.
9. Serve all operating zones as tasked. Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Zone C is the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks. Zone D is the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Zone F holds the value-added services area.
10. Respect storage limits in Zone B. The high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions. Each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg. A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg. Free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height and must not exceed 3 pallets high.
11. Handle hazardous loads only under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. The hazmat cage is inside Zone F and covers 60 m2. No more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, which holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.
12. Report to shift control. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Escalate defects, damage and unsafe conditions immediately and stop the affected truck or operation until cleared.

diff.title: Dispatch Capacity and Release
diff.before:
1. Harborwick provides outbound staging in Zone D in front of docks 5-8 for all scheduled dispatches. Operationally staging capacity is managed to keep staged pallets clear of dock approaches and available for prompt loading. Reliably staged loads are released in door call order to avoid congestion.

2. Altogether the building operates 8 dock doors with maintained access for concurrent inbound and outbound work. Specifically dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch and are reserved for loading and departure activities. Four outbound dock doors remain dedicated to outbound schedules during staffed shifts.

3. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads under client bookings. Carriers receive assigned doors and time slots from the dispatcher before arrival. Timely communication of slot changes keeps waiting time to a minimum.

6. Contracted curtain-side trailers carry a payload of 24000 kg for outbound consignments. Aboard each trailer there are 33 floor pallet positions for floor-loaded pallets. Safely loaded quantity respects both payload and floor-position limits on every departure.

7. Given a maximum pallet gross weight of 1000 kg including its load, a trailer takes at most 24 full-weight pallets. Therefore outbound capacity reaches at most 288 full-weight pallets per shift across doors, loads and trailer limits. Fully laden shipments approaching these limits are planned across multiple trailers.

8. Complementing trailers, our delivery van carries a payload of 1200 kg for smaller consignments. Inside the van there are 6 pallet positions for light orders. Consequently the van takes at most 1 full-weight pallets; heavier orders go by trailer.

9. Before release toward dispatch, PR-05 Packing and labelling applies to every order container. Picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing to confirm accuracy before cartons are closed. Afterwards PR-06 Outbound dispatch governs wrapping and load release and loading for all staged orders.

10. Using 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers, dispatch wraps every outbound pallet to stable transport condition. Moreover each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller supporting safe bridging between dock and trailer. Ultimately no load is released unless wrapping, documentation and dispatcher release are complete.

diff.title: Operating Hours and Cut-offs
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. operates the warehouse on two staffed shifts, Monday to Friday.
2. Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and provides full receiving, storage, picking and dispatch coverage.
3. Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, and provides continued receiving, picking, packing and dispatch coverage.
4. Outside these staffed hours no inbound or outbound handling is committed unless additional working has been expressly agreed.
5. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime, and any agreed extension will be confirmed with its supervised hours.
6. The building has 8 dock doors available for scheduled carrier movements within the operating shifts.
7. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving under PR-01 Inbound receiving.
8. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
9. There are 4 outbound dock doors, and outbound capacity is planned exclusively against those doors.
10. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers for both inbound and outbound movements.
11. Carriers must arrive within the assigned slot, as late arrival may require rescheduling to the next available door and slot.
12. For inbound receiving, the agreed intake cut-off means booked arrivals received before the cut-off enter same-shift inspection and system booking.
13. Booked arrivals received after the applicable intake cut-off will be received and processed on the next staffed shift.

diff.title: Picking and Packing Accuracy
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. maintains Zone C as the picking zone with ground-level pick faces and flow racks, operated exclusively through scanner-directed tasks. Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks and no order is picked from paper lists or memory.

2. Pick-face availability is guaranteed under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces. Harborwick commits that pick faces are replenished BEFORE the picking shift starts, so each shift begins with saleable stock presented at the face. Bulk reserve remains behind the flow lanes until transferred by replenishment.

3. Order execution is guaranteed under PR-04 Order picking. Every pick is directed by the warehouse management system to a specific location in Zone C. The client receives scan-verified picks where quantity, SKU and location are confirmed in the system at the face.

4. Picking accuracy is supported by a shared pool of 20 handheld WMS scanners for pickers and inbound staff. Harborwick commits to provide charged, functional scanners for every active picking assignment and to withdraw any faulty unit from use until checked.

5. Harborwick commits that picked items are scan-verified BEFORE packing under PR-04 Order picking and PR-05 Packing and labelling. No container passes to packing benches without completed system verification of its contents against the order.

6. Packing and labelling performance is guaranteed under PR-05 Packing and labelling. Harborwick commits to pack, seal, label and check every order container before release toward dispatch. Each parcel and pallet load leaves packing with correct customer labels, shipping marks and documentation inserts.

7. Outbound pallets built from picked orders comply with a maximum gross weight of 1000 kg per pallet, including its load. Harborwick commits to weigh-check pallet builds during packing and to split or reconfigure any build that would exceed 1000 kg before staging.

8. Dispatch uses 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers to stabilise palletised orders after packing. Harborwick commits to wrap every outbound pallet to base-to-top stability before transfer from packing toward staging.

9. Harborwick maintains Zone D as the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Packed, labelled and wrapped orders are staged in Zone D by outbound load and door call, protected from damage and ready for collection.

10. For the duration of this agreement Harborwick commits to operate replenishment, picking and packing as one controlled chain. Replenishment under PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces enables picking under PR-04 Order picking, verified picking enables work under PR-05 Packing and labelling, and only packed, labelled and weight-compliant pallets enter Zone D for dispatch.

diff.title: Put-away and Storage Accuracy
diff.before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. commits to accurate put-away of all booked inventory under PR-02 Put-away to storage.
2. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A before any storage movement begins.
3. Within receiving, inspection of inbound goods is completed before booking into the system.
4. Following system booking, goods are released for put-away to storage without interim diversion.
5. Through this sequence the client receives full system traceability from dock receipt to final storage location.

6. Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
7. Across that zone the high-bay racking provides 2,400 pallet positions dedicated to client stock.
8. Against every position Harborwick records pallet identity, SKU, quantity and bay location at the time of put-away.
9. Accordingly the client inventory remains system-directed, with no unbooked pallets held in bulk storage.

10. For weight control a pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 1000 kg.
11. Beyond pallet level each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg.
12. Inside bulk storage consignments exceeding bay capacity are split before put-away to protect rack integrity.
13. Consequently storage accuracy includes continuous compliance with both pallet and bay weight limits.

14. Where free block stacking applies, stacked pallets must not exceed 4.0 m in height.
15. Separately free block-stacked pallets must not exceed 3 pallets high.
16. Both height and quantity limits are applied together during put-away planning and floor verification.
17. Toward accuracy assurance, any stack found outside either limit is corrected and rebooked before acceptance as stored.

18. Ultimately Harborwick warrants that booked goods are put away to the assigned Zone B location, within stated rack and stacking limits, with system accuracy maintained from booking through storage.

diff.title: Aisles, walkways and speed limits
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse on every movement inside the building, in the outdoor yard and on all dock approaches.
2. Drive all handling equipment within the posted limits at all times without exception.
3. Do not exceed 10 km/h inside the building.
Reduce speed early before entering doorways, bends, intersections and areas with restricted visibility, and give way to pedestrians at every crossing.
4. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
Adjust speed further for wet surfaces, darkness, glare and yard traffic, and keep to the marked driving lanes.
5. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings.
Stop where sight lines are blocked, make eye contact with pedestrians before proceeding, and sound the horn where the layout requires it.
6. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
Approach levellers squarely, check that the leveller plate is seated and secure, and do not mount or cross a leveller showing a fault or warning tag.
7. Use main transport aisles as the primary travel routes for longitudinal movement.
Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide.
Keep both sides clear of pallets, packaging, chargers and staged equipment, and never park or double-handle loads in them.
8. Enter rack storage aisles only for put-away, replenishment or picking tasks.
Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide.
Proceed at walking pace where the aisle is occupied, check both ends before entering, and reverse out only with a banksman or mirrors where rear visibility is limited.
9. Keep segregated pedestrian walkways exclusively for foot traffic.
Segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide.
Never place pallets, pallet jacks, waste or tools in walkways, never cut across them with a truck, and cross them only at the marked crossings after slowing to the pedestrian-zone limit.
10. Maintain separation between trucks and pedestrians at interfaces.
Yield to foot traffic at walkway crossings, keep forks low and the load stable when passing, and stop the truck completely when a pedestrian steps into the travel path.
11. Report faded floor markings, damaged barriers, blocked walkways and defective speed signage immediately for repair.
Treat any unmarked or unclear section as a pedestrian area until markings are restored, and operate at the lower speed limit in the meantime.
12. Enforce these limits during congestion, shift changes and peak dispatch activity.
Slow down rather than overtake in narrow sections, queue in the direction of travel, and wait for the aisle to clear before entering with a loaded pallet.

diff.title: Safe operation rules
diff.before:
1. Wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Fasten the belt before selecting direction and keep it fastened until the truck is fully parked with the brake applied. Never override, bridge or remove the belt interlock.

2. Complete the documented daily check before first use each day under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

Withdraw any truck with defective brakes, steering, horn, lights, seat belt, forks, chains or tyres from service immediately. Report the defect for repair and take a serviceable truck instead.

3. Observe the indoor limit inside the building.

Drive forklifts at no more than 10 km/h in all indoor aisles, storage areas and handling zones. Adjust further down for congestion, floor conditions, visibility and load stability.

4. Limit speed in the outdoor yard to the posted yard maximum.

Drive at no more than 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, including trailer manoeuvring areas and routes to the dock approaches. Increase following distances on wet, icy or uneven surfaces.

5. Reduce speed to 5 km/h in every marked pedestrian zone and at every marked pedestrian crossing.

Anticipate pedestrians at aisle ends, doorways, staging areas and crossings even where markings are worn. Sound the horn at blind corners and stop where sight lines are blocked.

6. Approach every dock ramp and leveller approach at crawling speed.

Drive at no more than 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches, square to the leveller and without sharp steering on the slope. Confirm the leveller, dock seal and restraint are correctly set before driving on or off the trailer bed.

7. Maintain full control of the load on all routes.

Travel with forks low, mast tilted back and load against the backrest, looking in the direction of travel. Reverse where the load blocks forward vision, use a banksman where local rules require it, and never carry passengers or lift persons unless the equipment is specifically approved for that task.

8. Give way to pedestrians everywhere and stop rather than edge past.

Keep clear of the segregated walkways, halt at crossings, and wait until pedestrians have cleared the manoeuvring envelope before proceeding. Lower the forks, neutralise controls and apply the parking brake before stepping off, even for brief stops.

9. Park only in designated areas without obstructing aisles, doors, emergency routes or charging points.

Remove the key, apply the parking brake and lower the forks fully to the floor on shutdown. Report every contact, tip, slip or near miss on the shift so the truck can be rechecked before return to work.

diff.title: Walkways, aisles and dock areas
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse in all shared traffic areas. Keep forklift and pedestrian movements separated wherever marked routes exist.

2. Use only marked segregated pedestrian walkways for walking through the warehouse. Those walkways are 1.2 m wide and are separated from truck routes by markings and barriers where installed.

3. Do not step outside walkways or designated crossings to take shortcuts across aisles. Wait behind the marked line at crossings until the forklift operator has acknowledged you and stopped.

4. Wear high-visibility vests at all times on the warehouse floor. No person may enter floor, aisle or dock areas without a high-visibility vest and safety footwear class S3.

5. Drive centrally in main transport aisles and expect two-way truck traffic. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and must be kept clear of pallets, waste and staged goods at all times.

6. Control speed strictly by location. Forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

7. Reduce speed to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings. Give way to every pedestrian and stop completely where sight lines are restricted.

8. Enter rack storage aisles with caution and reduced speed. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; do not overtake, do not park, and sound the horn before entering blind aisle ends.

9. The building has 8 dock doors. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving in Zone A, covering unloading and goods inspection. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch in Zone D, covering outbound staging in front of the doors.

10. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller; check the leveller is correctly seated before driving on or off the trailer.

11. Observe dock discipline at Zone A and Zone D. Do not approach an open door, enter a trailer, or start loading or unloading until authorised. Keep dock staging clear of walkways and crossings.

12. Follow all instructions from dispatchers at the docks. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads, and the dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers.

13. Direct visiting drivers to the designated waiting location and keep them clear of manoeuvring trucks. Do not allow drivers to walk the floor unescorted or to enter Zone A or Zone D without high-visibility vests and safety footwear class S3.

14. Report blocked walkways, damaged barriers, faded markings, faulty dock levellers or unsafe staging to supervision immediately. Do not resume normal traffic through the affected area until it has been cleared and released.

diff.title: Driver authorisation and truck checks
diff.before:
1. Operate material-handling equipment only under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and only if you are an authorised operator. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.

2. Obtain authorisation before driving any powered truck. Only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

3. Remember that the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs. Do not permit unauthorised driving, passengers, or use of a truck reported as faulty.

4. Know the fleet you are assigned to. The fleet has 6 electric counterbalance forklifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 2.5 t.

2. Complete the documented pre-use check each day. Every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day, and the daily forklift check happens BEFORE first use each day.

diff.title: Common Rules and Training
diff.before:
1. Report through the on-duty chain on every shift: each employee reports to the shift supervisor running the shift, and the shift supervisor reports to the warehouse manager.
2. Under this structure the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, while the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
3. Work the published roster pattern covering the 6,000 m2 floor: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. Obtain cover for any additional hours in advance, as only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Wear issued personal protective equipment at all times on the warehouse floor: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
6. Keep to segregated routes and clearances: main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide.
7. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse whenever leaving a walkway, making eye contact with drivers before crossing and using only marked pedestrian zones and crossings.
8. Within PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, respect all posted limits: forklifts must not exceed 10 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
9. Reduce speed further at interfaces: forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
10. Fasten restraint systems without exception: forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and no new driver may operate until only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators has been satisfied.

13. Protect temperature-sensitive stock to specification: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.
14. Respect hazardous-storage discipline: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, with access limited to trained and authorised personnel.

diff.title: Hall, yard and zones overview
diff.before:
1. The Harborwick site centres on a single warehouse hall covering 6,000 m2, with an adjoining outdoor yard for manoeuvring and parking. Learn the hall perimeter, the yard entrances and the marked internal routes before starting work.
2. Eight dock doors serve the building on one facade. Dock doors 1-4 are assigned to inbound receiving, while dock doors 5-8 are assigned to outbound dispatch, including 4 outbound dock doors available for loading.
3. Zone A forms the receiving zone at inbound docks 1-4. All unloading and goods inspection takes place there, and inbound vehicles are marshalled to those four doors only.
4. From Zone A, approved stock moves directly into storage. Zone B provides bulk storage in high-bay pallet racking, which offers 2,400 pallet positions across the high bays.
5. Zone C operates as the picking zone. It contains ground-level pick faces and flow racks arranged for short travel and scanner-directed work, separate from the high-bay reserve in Zone B.
6. Zone D provides the dispatch zone for outbound staging in front of docks 5-8. Build and check outbound loads there, keeping each door apron clear for the next trailer.
7. Zone E is the cold zone for chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Access is restricted to assigned tasks, and doors are kept closed except for put-away and retrieval.
8. Zone F holds the value-added services area. Inside Zone F, a fenced hazmat cage covers 60 m2 for segregated storage, alongside the designated areas for quarantine and rework.
9. Main transport aisles through the hall measure 4.0 m wide. Keep them free of pallets, waste and staged stock at all times to allow two-way truck movement.
10. Rack storage aisles between the high bays measure 3.0 m wide. Enter them only when authorised, observe priority signs, and never stage pallets inside the aisle profile.
11. Pedestrian routes cross the hall at defined points and connect all zones A-F. Use only those routes when moving on foot, remain clear of truck swept paths, and report any blocked or faded markings.
12. Memorise the zone sequence from goods-in to goods-out: Zone A for receiving at doors 1-4, Zone B for bulk storage, Zone C for picking, Zone D for dispatch at doors 5-8, Zone E for chilled storage, and Zone F for value-added services including the hazmat cage.

diff.title: Put-away process
diff.before:
1. Execute PR-02 Put-away to storage for every pallet released from receiving and move only system-booked goods to their storage destination.

2. Confirm in the WMS that inbound goods were inspected before booking, because inspection always precedes system booking, and never start put-away when the booking receipt is missing or incomplete.

3. Release pallets to put-away strictly after system booking, since goods are booked into the system before put-away to storage, and return any unbooked pallet to receiving for completion of the inbound steps.

4. Assign Forklift operators to all put-away transport, as Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks, and select the truck type that suits the pallet weight, height and destination aisle.

5. Direct ambient bulk pallets to Zone B, noting that Zone B is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking, and follow the WMS location instruction for aisle, bay and level without substituting an alternative position.

6. Transport chilled pallets immediately to Zone E, noting that Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C, and minimise door-open and staging time to protect the temperature range.

7. Deliver pallets requiring labelling, kitting, inspection or other special treatment to Zone F, noting that Zone F holds the value-added services area, and hand over each pallet to the responsible staff at the defined drop point.

8. Scan every put-away at the destination location and verify that the WMS confirms the correct zone and position for Zone B, Zone E or Zone F.

9. Report missing labels, unreadable barcodes, damaged pallets or occupied locations immediately and leave the pallet in a safe holding position until the system instruction is corrected.

10. Close PR-02 Put-away to storage in the WMS only after all pallets from the booking have a confirmed storage location, thereby keeping booked stock, physical location and system inventory fully aligned for replenishment and picking.

11. Keep put-away lanes and staging areas clear during the operation and return handling equipment to its parking position once the last pallet of the booking is stored.

diff.title: Cold storage in Zone E
diff.before:
1. Hold all chilled stock only in Zone E in line with PR-12 Cold-chain handling.
2. Maintain Zone E within its chilled range at all times during storage and put-away.
3. Verify the cold-zone temperature manually each shift and record the reading.
4. Prioritise cold-chain pallets at put-away and minimise time outside Zone E.
5. Segregate non-conforming chilled stock immediately and escalate under PR-12 Cold-chain handling.

Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Do not use Zone E for ambient, quarantine or general bulk overflow. Keep the boundary to the rest of the warehouse closed except for direct put-away, replenishment and collection moves.

6. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C. Treat any reading below +2 °C as a breach.
7. Keep the cold zone at or below +8 °C. Treat any reading above +8 °C as a breach.
8. Check the fixed display on entry and confirm it with the manual verification for the shift.
9. Log each shift verification with time and initials in the designated record.
10. Re-verify after any prolonged door opening, defrost cycle or maintenance work.

Manual verification each shift is mandatory and does not replace continuous monitoring where fitted. Never rely on memory or on the previous shift reading. Record the actual observed value at the time of the check and sign for it.

11. Move chilled inbound pallets to Zone E without delay after release from receiving.
12. Transport chilled goods in closed load units and do not stage them in ambient aisles.
13. Rotate chilled stock by expiry date and keep labels visible for scanner tasks.
14. Leave air circulation gaps around pallets and do not block coolers or sensors.
15. Keep Zone E floors dry, clear of packaging waste and free of ice build-up.

Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every receipt, put-away, replenishment, pick and return that touches chilled product. Follow its steps for temperature evidence, time limits outside the chamber and handling of insulated containers. Where PR-12 Cold-chain handling requires a hold, place the stock on hold and prevent further picking until release.

16. Stop normal put-away into Zone E on any temperature breach and contain stock already inside.
17. Quarantine product exposed to out-of-range conditions pending a documented decision.
18. Report every breach, probe failure and missing shift check without delay for review.
19. Do not release breached chilled stock to picking, packing or dispatch without authorisation.
20. Restore the +2 to +8 °C range and prove stability with a fresh verification before resuming normal moves.

Discipline in Zone E protects product safety and stock accuracy. Maintain the +2 to +8 °C envelope, verify it manually each shift, work strictly to PR-12 Cold-chain handling, and keep full records to show the cold chain was never broken.

diff.title: Cold-chain and hazmat controls
diff.before:
1. Execute PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all chilled stock movements, storage and temperature checks without exception.
2. Maintain Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C for all temperature-controlled inventory.
3. Verify the Zone E temperature manually each shift with the calibrated display and site thermometer.
4. Record each shift reading immediately in the temperature log with time and initials.
5. Keep the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
6. Keep the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times during storage, replenishment and picking.
7. Close Zone E doors promptly after every entry and exit to protect the +2 to +8 °C range.
8. Isolate any pallet showing temperature abuse and escalate it under PR-12 Cold-chain handling before further movement.
9. Prohibit staging chilled pallets outside Zone E except for immediate loading or put-away under active control.
10. Execute PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for all classified hazardous goods, storage checks and spill actions.
11. Store all hazmat only inside the fenced hazmat cage inside Zone F, never in general racking or open floor areas.
12. Limit total holdings in the hazmat cage to no more than 4,000 kg at one time across all SKUs and containers.
13. Plan cage occupancy on the basis that the hazmat cage holds at most 4 full-weight pallets.
14. Check cage stock weight before every put-away and reject any receipt that would exceed 4,000 kg.
15. Keep incompatible classes segregated within the cage according to label instructions and PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
16. Inspect containers, bunds, labels and extinguishers each shift and clear any obstruction from cage access and spill kits.
17. Contain drips immediately, ventilate the area, don the specified protective equipment and notify supervision under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response.
18. Forbid ignition sources, food and unauthorised entry inside the cage and ensure spill residues leave only through the approved waste route.

diff.title: Cold zone rules
diff.before:
1. Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling to every pallet, carton and tote stored in Zone E.

Zone E is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Treat any deviation from that band as a cold-chain failure, not as a local fluctuation. Never store ambient, frozen or uncontrolled goods in Zone E to save space or time.

2. Maintain the cold zone at or above +2 °C at all times.

Monitor door openings, defrost cycles and loading dwell times because each one drives temperature downward or disrupts airflow. Keep the doors closed except for active put-away, replenishment or loading, and report icing, pooling water or uneven cooling without delay.

3. Maintain the cold zone at or below +8 °C at all times.

During warm weather, frequent access or equipment heat can push the upper limit quickly. Limit personnel entry to assigned tasks, switch off idle handling equipment inside the chamber, and escalate any upward trend before the limit is reached.

4. Verify cold-zone temperature manually each shift.

Use the calibrated display and the manual check defined in PR-12 Cold-chain handling, then record the reading, time and your name in the designated log. Across shift changes, communicate the last verified reading and any door or plant faults as part of handover.

5. Wear mandatory protection before entering Zone E.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor, including all work inside the cold zone. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor, including wet or cold floors in Zone E. Add suitable thermal layers and gloves for prolonged chilled work, keeping cuffs, laces and hems clear of pallets and rollers.

6. Control movements and behaviour inside the chilled area.

Walk at a steady pace on potentially slippery surfaces, use handrails where provided, and never run to warm up. Handle chilled cartons with dry hands or appropriate gloves, stack them stably, and clean up condensation or spillages immediately to prevent slips.

7. Protect product integrity during every transfer.

Plan picks and put-aways so chilled goods remain inside Zone E until the moment of movement. Stage outbound chilled pallets only for immediate loading and return inbound chilled pallets to Zone E without intermediate storage in ambient areas.

8. Escalate alarms, suspect stock and equipment faults immediately.

Notify the shift supervisor, who runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, of any temperature alarm, door failure, refrigeration fault, or pallet that feels warm, thawed or damp. Isolate suspect stock as directed under PR-12 Cold-chain handling and prevent its picking, packing or dispatch until cleared.

9. Keep accountability for cold-chain safety unambiguous.

The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, including calibration, maintenance priorities and final decisions on temperature-abused stock. The shift supervisor controls chilled work on the shift, enforces PR-12 Cold-chain handling, confirms each manual verification, and ensures only fit staff work extended periods in low temperatures.

diff.title: Shift Supervisors
diff.before:
1. Run one assigned shift in full charge of floor staff and incident response.
2. Direct Shift 1 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday, according to roster.
3. Report to the warehouse manager, who remains accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
4. Allocate inbound operators, forklift operators, pickers, stock controllers, returns staff, maintenance support and dispatch activity for the shift.
5. Supervise Zone A, the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection.
6. Supervise Zone B, the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking.
7. Supervise Zone C, the picking zone: ground-level pick faces and flow racks.
8. Supervise Zone D, the dispatch zone: outbound staging in front of docks 5-8.
9. Supervise Zone E, the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C.
10. Supervise Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.
11. Enforce mandatory high-visibility vests for everyone on the warehouse floor.
12. Enforce mandatory safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor.
13. Review every incident report arising on the shift and direct immediate containment, first response and escalation.
14. Lead evacuation under PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
15. Control the quarterly evacuation drill on shift, account for all personnel at the assembly point and ensure roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.
16. Approve damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling.
17. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval before any system posting.
18. Approve the final disposition of inspected returns under PR-07 Returns handling, confirming restock, rework or scrap.
19. Execute PR-15 End-of-shift handover at every change of shift and remain accountable until the incoming shift supervisor has accepted the floor in person.
20. Brief the incoming supervisor on labour, equipment status, overdue orders, cold-zone integrity, quarantine holdings, incidents and open safety actions.

During the shift the supervisor stays visible on the floor, prioritises safety over throughput and stops any unsafe operation. Absences, equipment faults and zone congestion are rebalanced across Zones A to F without delaying outbound commitments. diff.title: Inbound Operators
diff.before:
1. Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A and execute PR-01 Inbound receiving from document check to system booking.

Zone A is the receiving zone: inbound docks 1-4, unloading and goods inspection. The building has 8 dock doors, of which dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Operators report for their assigned shift, either Shift 1 which runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, or Shift 2 which runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.

2. Before any trailer is opened, verify the booking, delivery note and purchase order quantity against the scheduled load.

At receiving, the document check happens BEFORE unloading. Do not start unloading where documents are missing, quantities disagree or damage is visible from outside until the exception has been escalated under PR-01 Inbound receiving.

3. During unloading, count every carton and pallet, check outer packaging condition, labels and expiry dates where applicable, and segregate quantity variances and visible damage.

Inbound goods are inspected BEFORE they are booked into the system. Record inspection results in the WMS and on the delivery paperwork without delay.

4. Operate pallet handling equipment within the receiving area to move inbound pallets to inspection and booking lanes, keeping pedestrian routes and dock approaches clear at all times.

Pickers and inbound staff share 20 handheld WMS scanners. Sign out a scanner at shift start, confirm each booking scan, and return the unit for charging at shift end.

5. Book inspected goods into the system immediately after inspection, print or activate pallet labels, and confirm weight and dimensions.

A pallet, including its load, may weigh at most 900 kg. Reject overweight or unstable pallets for rework before booking.

6. Stage booked pallets by destination for release to PR-02 Put-away to storage.

Goods are booked into the system BEFORE put-away to storage. Direct general pallets for Zone B, which is the bulk storage zone: high-bay pallet racking. Direct chilled pallets for Zone E, which is the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +8 °C. Direct value-added, quarantine and returns-related receipts for Zone F, which holds the value-added services area.

7. Hand over staged stock to forklift operators for put-away only after system booking is complete, ensuring each pallet carries its identifier and destination.

Never release unbooked goods to storage aisles or dispatch areas.

8. Wear prescribed personal protective equipment throughout all receiving work.

High-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.

9. Work under the direction of the shift team structure at all times.

The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response. Follow tasking, report variances, damage and missing documents immediately, and request reassignment before leaving Zone A. The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

diff.title: Common Rules and Training
diff.before:
1. Report through the on-duty chain on every shift: each employee reports to the shift supervisor running the shift, and the shift supervisor reports to the warehouse manager.
2. Under this structure the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs, while the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
3. Work the published roster pattern covering the 6,000 m2 floor: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
4. Obtain cover for any additional hours in advance, as only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
5. Wear issued personal protective equipment at all times on the warehouse floor: high-visibility vests are mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor and safety footwear class S3 is mandatory on the warehouse floor.
6. Keep to segregated routes and clearances: main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide, and segregated pedestrian walkways are 1.2 m wide.
7. Observe PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse whenever leaving a walkway, making eye contact with drivers before crossing and using only marked pedestrian zones and crossings.
8. Within PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation, respect all posted limits: forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and must not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.
9. Reduce speed further at interfaces: forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
10. Fasten restraint systems without exception: forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, and no new driver may operate until only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators has been satisfied.
11. Complete mandatory training before unsupervised work: PR-01 Inbound receiving, PR-02 Put-away to storage, PR-03 Replenishment of pick faces, PR-04 Order picking, PR-05 Packing and labelling, and PR-06 Outbound dispatch.
12. Maintain competence in support and safety procedures: PR-07 Returns handling, PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, PR-12 Cold-chain handling, PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response, PR-14 Emergency evacuation, and PR-15 End-of-shift handover.
13. Protect temperature-sensitive stock to specification: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and must stay at or below +8 °C, with cold-zone temperature manually verified each shift.
14. Respect hazardous-storage discipline: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time, with access limited to trained and authorised personnel.
15. Attend the evacuation drill that runs every quarter, follow the marshalled route to the assembly point, and remain there because roll call at the assembly point happens BEFORE anyone re-enters the building.

diff.title: Approvals and ownership
diff.before:
1. Stocktake results remain under single ownership. Only the warehouse manager may sign off stocktake results.

Under PR-08 Stocktaking and cycle counts, stock controllers prepare counts, recounts and adjustments for review. Submit the completed stocktake file for warehouse-manager sign-off before any final posting. Do not treat a shift-level check as final approval.

2. Damaged-goods write-offs follow a fixed monetary threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval.

Apply the threshold to each write-off proposal separately under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling. Record the estimated value, cause and supporting inspection notes in the system. Route any case above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager without exception.

3. Lower-value write-offs stay with shift leadership. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR.

Within that limit, the shift supervisor confirms quantity, value and disposal method. Forward the approved record to stock control for system adjustment. Escalate any doubtful valuation before approval.

4. Larger losses require senior sign-off. The warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR.

At this level the warehouse manager verifies evidence, decides on further investigation and authorises disposal or claim action. Retain the signed approval with the damaged-goods record in Zone F quarantine documentation. Do not scrap or release goods pending this decision.

5. Returns decisions have a separate owner. The shift supervisor approves the final disposition of inspected returns.

Under PR-07 Returns handling, returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap. Present the inspection result and recommendation to the shift supervisor for decision. Implement restock, rework or scrap only after that approval.

6. Overtime cannot be authorised on the floor. Only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.

diff.before:

10. Release approved rework units to the rework area in Zone F and return them to inspection on completion before any restock booking.
11. Value every scrap and damaged-goods proposal in EUR at cost price before seeking write-off approval.
12. Obtain shift supervisor approval for damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR and record the approval, value and reason in the system.

diff.title: Damaged goods and quarantine
diff.before:
1. Execute PR-09 Damaged-goods handling for every unit found broken, leaking, crushed, contaminated, wet, or otherwise unfit for normal storage or sale.

2. Transfer the affected unit to quarantine on the same shift it is discovered, without waiting for valuation or approval. During storage and returns work, place damaged stock on a pallet or in a containment tray to prevent further spillage.

3. Isolate all quarantine stock physically inside the quarantine area in Zone F. Never leave damaged goods in receiving, bulk, picking, dispatch, or traffic aisles while awaiting a decision.

4. Attach a quarantine tag at the time of transfer. Record the date, time, SKU, quantity, location of discovery, type of damage, name of the discoverer, and pallet identifier where applicable.

5. Enter the quarantine movement in the system immediately after the physical transfer. Keep the stock blocked from sale, replenishment, picking, and dispatch until formally released or written off.

6. Photograph the damage before any repacking or sorting. Retain the photographs with the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling record for audit and claim use.

7. Assess whether partial salvage is possible. Separate intact inner units from destroyed outer packaging only inside Zone F, and return only clean and fully saleable units to the inspection flow.

8. Value the proposed write-off at cost price in EUR. Prepare one write-off request per incident, listing SKU, quantity, unit cost, total value, cause, and attached photographs.

9. Submit write-offs valued up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for decision. Do not scrap, destroy, or adjust the system until the shift supervisor approves the write-off.

10. Escalate write-offs valued above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for decision. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and system adjustment or destruction must wait for that approval.

11. Respect the accountability structure on every case. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR, and the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.

12. Carry out the approved outcome without delay. Release salvageable stock through the system, send scrap for destruction through the defined waste route, and file the signed approval with the quarantine log.

13. Review quarantine holdings each working day. Chase overdue valuations, missing photographs, and pending approvals so that no damaged pallet remains in the quarantine area in Zone F longer than operationally necessary.

14. Prohibit unauthorised removal from quarantine. Release stock only on documented approval, and record the name of the approver, the quantity released, and the destination on the PR-09 Damaged-goods handling form.

diff.title: Spills, quarantine and damage
diff.before:
1. Contain every spill immediately under PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response. Stop the source if safe to do so, cordon the affected floor area, prevent liquid reaching drains and aisles, and alert surrounding staff without leaving the hazard unattended.

2. During any spill response wear high-visibility vests as mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor. Keep safety footwear class S3 mandatory on the warehouse floor laced and intact, and add task-specific protection required by PR-13 before handling spilled containers, absorbents or contaminated packaging.

3. Notify the shift supervisor at once for any injury, near miss, spill, damaged racking or unsafe behaviour. The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, takes control of the scene, decides on isolation, ventilation or evacuation of the immediate area, and coordinates clean-up and disposal.

4. Record every spill and contamination event in an incident report before the end of the shift. Describe substance, quantity, location, persons exposed, containment actions and photographs where taken, and submit the report for review without delay.

5. Ensure the shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Check that containment was complete, that waste was segregated correctly, that affected stock was identified, and that corrective actions for cleaning, retraining or equipment repair are assigned and closed.

6. Transfer all damaged, leaking, suspect-temperature or contaminated units to quarantine in Zone F without exception. Handle damaged goods thereafter only under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling, keeping quarantine stock physically separated, clearly labelled and excluded from saleable inventory until formally released.

7. Remember that Zone F holds the value-added services area. Carry out inspection, sorting, repacking assessment, photography and valuation only inside the quarantine area in Zone F, maintaining clear access for inspection and preventing mixing with conforming VAS work.

8. Photograph damage before repacking or sorting, preserve labels and batch data, and value each damaged-goods proposal at cost price. Segregate intact inner units from destroyed packaging, retain samples where required, and prepare the written recommendation for restock, rework or scrap.

9. Obtain write-off approval before scrapping or adjusting any damaged stock. The shift supervisor approves damaged-goods write-offs up to 500 EUR, recorded with quantity, value, reason and supporting photographs.

10. Escalate larger losses to the warehouse manager without splitting consignments to avoid the threshold. Damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR need warehouse-manager approval, and the warehouse manager approves damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR only on documented evidence and completed quarantine inspection.

11. Release quarantine holdings only after inspection, approval and system clearance. Return conforming stock to its assigned location, route rework through re-inspection, dispose of scrap through the approved waste stream, and file approvals with incident and stock records for audit.

diff.title: Reporting incidents
diff.before:
1. Report every injury, near miss, collision, dropped pallet, rack strike, spill, fire alarm activation and equipment fault without delay.
2. Notify the shift supervisor immediately from the scene by radio, telephone or in person and secure the area against further movement.
3. Remember the shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response, and remains your first point of contact for any unsafe condition.
4. Complete the incident report form before leaving the shift, giving time, exact location, persons involved, equipment involved, witnesses and a factual description of what happened.
5. Forward each completed report to the shift supervisor for review on the same shift, as the shift supervisor reviews every incident report.
6. Preserve evidence until released by supervision: do not move damaged racking, spilt product, broken pallets or vehicles except to prevent immediate danger.
7. Transfer damaged stock to the quarantine area in Zone F and identify each pallet or carton with date, location found, incident reference and reporter name.
8. Handle all damage valuation, photography and disposition under PR-09 Damaged-goods handling and do not scrap, rework or restock affected units without written approval.
9. Obtain approval for every damaged-goods write-off before posting any adjustment in the system.
10. Submit write-offs up to 500 EUR to the shift supervisor for approval and retain the signed valuation with the incident file.
11. Escalate damaged-goods write-offs above 500 EUR to the warehouse manager for approval, since the warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
12. Attach the approval, photographs, scanner records and quarantine transfer note to the incident report for audit.
13. Include all open incidents, injuries, damage transfers to quarantine and pending write-off approvals in PR-15 End-of-shift handover to the incoming shift supervisor.
14. Monitor corrective actions assigned at handover until closed and report any recurrence, failed containment or missing approval to supervision immediately.

diff.title: Shift Supervisors
diff.before:
